thread.title: Here’s when history suggests Apple’s stock would be due for a pullback

author: Victor Reklaitis and Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Here’s when history suggests Apple’s stock would be due for a pullback
text:
The rally for U.S. equities isn’t letting up so far in the new year, but strategists continue to wave caution flags.
The biggest stock by market capitalization — Apple AAPL, -0.37% — can’t avoid selloffs after its advances, notes Sean Emory, founder and chief investment officer at Avory & Co.
His chart below shows drawdowns — the drops from a peak to a low — since 2004 for the Dow component. The graphic serves as our Need to Know column’s chart of the day .
Even the winners have bad days. “This is arguably the most important company of our generation and maybe all time, yet in its third decade of existence, the market still sends it lower by 30% every 2.8 years on average,” Emory tells MarketWatch.
The last drawdown of 30% or more for Apple’s stock took place between mid-2015 to mid-2016. That’s shown in the chart at the top of this article.
So if another 30% drawdown were to come 2.8 years after Apple’s 2016 trough, it would hit in early 2019.
In the new year, Apple has been dealing with criticism that its iPhone is addictive for children. A pair of prominent investors have called on the tech giant to do more on this issue, and the company has defended its record of providing parental controls and other protections.
Shares fell 0.4% on Monday, trimming their 12-month gain to 46.5%, but they were up 0.2% in premarket action on Tuesday.
Apple also has drawn flak lately for slowing down iPhones with older batteries, and it has apologized and offered a discount on some replacement batteries.
